description_full: Kanzhun Limited, together with its subsidiaries, operates an online recruitment platform in the People's Republic of China. It offers job seeking services that allow job seekers to receive job recommendations, initiate direct chats, and deliver resumes upon mutual consent, as well as value-added tools. The company also provides direct recruitment services to enterprise users to post jobs, receive personalized candidate recommendations, engage in direct communication, and receive resumes upon mutual consent. In addition, it offers online recruitment services through BOSS Zhipin, a mobile app; and management consultancy and technical services. Kanzhun Limited was founded in 2013 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

Revenue per employee of $238K ranks in the bottom quartile among Communication Services peers, with revenue growing 15%/yr across its filed history. CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: KANZHUN LIMITED - American Depo is a mid-cap communication services business with a $5.7B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +13.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 10% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $665M in free cash flow — roughly 54 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.66× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 3.5% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and stock-based comp at 11% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
